newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Treasury sees 1998 GDP growth of 3-3.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Israel Treasury sees 1998 GDP growth of 3-3.5 pct.

text.p: Israel's Treasury forecast on Thursday that economic growth would pick up in the second half of next year, with gross domestic product rising an estimated annual 3.0 to 3.5 percent.
GDP is expected to increase by only 2.5 percent in 1997.

The Treasury will present its economic forecast to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday and to the entire cabinet on Sunday, marking the start of its preparation of the 1998 budget. The Treasury will also review implementation of the 1997 budget.
On August 10 the cabinet will discuss the budget deficit target. The cabinet is expected to conclude discussion of the budget by September.
The budget deficit target next year will fall to 2.4 percent of GDP from 2.8 percent in 1997. The Treasury said it hoped to achieve this target without raising taxes.
Documents released by the Treasury on Thursday also showed two economic forecasts for 1999-2000. In the best case, GDP will grow by 5.4 percent annually and in the worst case by only 2.9 percent.
GDP per capita is expected to rise by 0.8-1.3 percent in 1998 against an estimated increase of only 0.2 percent this year. GDP per capita will reach $16,900 in 1997 and $17,500 in 1998.
